lessons.title: Fight for the centre
lessons.summary: Why central pawns and knights matter in the first moves.

steps.text: The four central squares (d4, e4, d5, e5) are the most valuable real estate on the board. Pieces placed there control the most squares.
Start by occupying the centre with a pawn — it frees your bishop and queen at the same time.
Black mirrored you. Now develop a piece toward the centre with tempo — attack the e5 pawn.
steps.task: Develop the king's knight with tempo

steps.text: Black defended with ...Nc6. Both sides now fight over d4/e5 — every developing move should add pressure on the centre.

lessons.title: Castle early
lessons.summary: Get the king out of the centre before the position opens.

steps.text: Both sides have developed their kingside pieces. The e-file may open soon — a king on e1 would be exposed.
Castle now: the king tucks away on g1 and the rook joins the game.
Done in one move: king safety plus a rook that can reach the centre files. Aim to castle within the first 10 moves in most openings.
Knights attack in an L-shape, and they can attack two pieces at once without being blocked. Look for squares that hit the king and another piece.
Find the square where the knight checks the king AND attacks the rook.
The king must move, and the knight takes the rook next move. Always check knight jumps that land with check.

lessons.title: Back-rank mate
lessons.summary: A king boxed in by its own pawns.

steps.text: Black's king is trapped behind its own pawns on f7, g7 and h7. If a rook or queen reaches the 8th rank with check, it is mate.
Checkmate. Defend against this in your own games by making 'luft' (h3/h6) or keeping a rook on the back rank.

lessons.title: Pin it
lessons.summary: Freeze a piece in front of its king.

steps.text: A pin attacks a piece that cannot move without exposing something more valuable behind it — here, the king on e8.
Line your bishop up with the knight and the king.
steps.task: Pin the knight to the king

steps.text: The knight on c6 is now absolutely pinned — it cannot legally move. Pile up on pinned pieces to win them.

lessons.title: Two-rook ladder mate
lessons.summary: Rooks working together on adjacent ranks.

steps.text: The rook on a7 cuts the king off on the 8th rank. The second rook only needs to give check on that rank.
Mate: one rook guards the 7th rank, the other checks on the 8th. The same 'ladder' works with queen + rook.
